Google Play, launch day

What are a new app's odds?

Pick what you'd know on the day an app launches. The model learned from Google Play apps launched from 2016 to 2021 and gives the chance of reaching 10K, 100K and 1M installs. It reads patterns in past apps. It can't tell you who will win.

Where it ends up among apps launched the same month

bottommediantop

Checked on apps it never saw. The 80% interval covered 80.1% of random held-out apps and 80.7% of launches after June 2019. It covers less for games (75.2%), and about 70% for Strategy and Action.

It is wide on purpose. On average the 80% interval spans 73% of the launch-month range, so for one app it gives a rough neighborhood and nothing sharper.

10K100K, dashed1M

One snapshot. The scrape sees each app once, in June 2021, so the time curve comes from comparing apps of different ages. It assumes launch cohorts grow at the same pace, which is only roughly true.

Forward check. Fit on launches before June 2019 and scored on the two years after, it ranked well (AUC 0.797 for 100K) but predicted too low, 2.7% against a real 3.6%. I'd treat the probabilities as rough.

    These are the real apps in the same category whose launch-day score sits closest to this one. Look at how far apart their installs are. Apps with the same profile land everywhere.

    Tap a row to switch category. Past apps only. Nothing here says what would happen if you picked a category.

    AssociationNone of this is in the model and none of it is advice. Monetization, privacy policy and website were read in June 2021, long after launch, and an app that already has users has every reason to add in-app purchases.
